name: Spine switch
kid: One of the big crossroads in the middle of the hall. Every cupboard has a road to every crossroad, so there are lots of equal roads and none of them gets jammed.
nerd: A spine of a leaf–spine (Clos) fabric: every leaf connects to every spine, so any two racks are two hops apart over many equal-cost paths. ECMP hashes each flow onto one of them.

1995.kid: Drawn as today. In 1995 a server room had one small hub, not big crossroads.
1995.nerd: Drawn as today: leaf–spine (Clos) fabrics became the norm in data centres in the 2010s. A 1995 server room had a 10 Mbit/s hub, or one of the first Ethernet switches.
